title: Chocolate Tofu Pudding with Candied Cacao Nibs + Banana

blocks.text: **Affiliate note:** Some links in this post may be affiliate links. If you buy through them, it helps support Date My Dish at no extra cost to you.

items: **What it is:** Silky chocolate tofu pudding (yes, tofu), topped with crunchy candied cacao nibs, sliced banana, and a tiny, grown-up drizzle of olive oil.
**Skill level:** Medium (caramel + candying vibes).
**Why it’s a date dish:** It’s rich and a little unexpected. Also, it’s mostly prep-ahead, so dessert lands with zero stress.

blocks.text: There’s a very specific kind of date-night confidence that comes from serving a dessert that feels like it belongs on a tasting menu.
Not fussy. Not fragile. Just sleek, glossy, and suspiciously good.

It’s a chocolate pudding that eats like pure indulgence, but the base is tofu and dates, which makes it feel light enough that you don’t immediately need a nap. The candied cacao nibs give you that crackly crunch. The banana adds sweetness and a soft bite. And the olive oil drizzle is the final “I know what I’m doing” move.

items: **Make-ahead friendly:** pudding and nibs can be done earlier.
**Big texture energy:** creamy + crunchy + chewy.
**Not too sweet:** the olive oil and salt keep it adult.
**It looks expensive** in a shallow bowl with one dramatic swirl.

blocks.text: **Template note:** This is written for **two generous servings**.

items: 90 g dates (about 6), pitted
120 g milk chocolate, chopped
1 pack silken/soft tofu (about 300–350 g), drained
1/2 tsp vanilla extract
1 Tbsp cacao powder (or Dutch-process cocoa)
1/4 tsp kosher salt
1 tsp extra virgin olive oil (plus extra for serving)
15 g cacao nibs
30 g sugar
3 g butter (about 3/4 tsp), cubed
1 banana, sliced (or 2 small bananas)
Flaky salt
A few fresh herbs (optional, but mint is cute)
Olive oil (a small drizzle)

blocks.text: Shopping Notes (So You Don’t Overthink It)

items: **Chocolate:** use a milk chocolate you’d eat straight. (If it’s very sweet, reduce the sugar in the candied nibs slightly.)
**Tofu:** use **silken/soft tofu** for the smoothest texture. Just drain it well so the pudding stays thick.
**Dates:** any pitted dates work. If your dates are dry, soaking matters.
**Bananas:** use ripe (yellow, lightly speckled) bananas for the best texture + sweetness.

blocks.text: Cover dates with **boiling water** and let them plump for **15 minutes**. Drain.
Melt the milk chocolate over a double boiler (or a heatproof bowl set over barely simmering water). Set aside to cool slightly.
Add drained dates and blend again until silky.
Add vanilla, cacao powder, salt, and olive oil. Blend until glossy and emulsified.
Press the mixture through a **fine-mesh sieve** into a bowl.
Stir in the melted chocolate until fully combined.
Portion into two serving bowls (or jars). Chill at least **30 minutes**.
Heat oven to **350°F / 177°C**. Spread cacao nibs on a tray and toast for **10 to 12 minutes**, until shiny and fragrant.
In a small saucepan over **medium-low**, add sugar and let it melt without stirring until it starts to caramelize. Once it’s mostly melted, gently stir until it reaches a **deep amber**.
Off heat, whisk in butter a cube at a time.
Stir in toasted nibs, then spread on parchment or a silicone mat. Cool until hard, then crush into bite-size pieces.
7) Assemble like you’re trying to impress (you are)
Spoon **2 heaping scoops** of pudding into a shallow bowl and swirl the surface with the back of a spoon.
Top with candied cacao nibs and a few banana slices.

items: a tiny drizzle of olive oil

**Ultra-smooth pudding:** sieve it. It’s the difference between “good” and “what is this sorcery.”
**Caramel fear:** if sugar is browning too fast, lower the heat and breathe.
**Banana timing:** slice right before serving so it stays fresh and doesn’t brown.
**Wine:** port, amaro, or a not-too-sweet red.
**Coffee:** espresso or strong pour-over.
**Fruit:** raspberries or strawberries if you want a little bright acidity.

blocks.text: Date Night Notes / During the Date
This dessert is built for a “we’re staying in, but it still feels special” kind of night.

items: **Lighting:** one lamp + one candle. No overhead lights.
**Music:** something low and smooth (jazz, R&B, or a “late-night dinner” playlist).
**Serving move:** use shallow bowls and do one dramatic swirl in the pudding. It’s the easiest plating trick that looks intentional.
**Before the date (earlier in the day):** make the pudding and chill it. Make candied cacao nibs and stash them in a jar.
**Right after dinner:** put the banana and topping ingredients on the counter. That’s it. You’re done “prep cooking.”
**During the date (the mini-activity):** crush candied nibs together and slice the bananas. It’s quick, low-mess, and still feels like you’re “doing something” together.
**Drink:** espresso, an amaro on ice, or a not-too-sweet red.
**Fruit sidecar (optional):** raspberries or strawberries.
**Salt + oil finish:** flaky salt is non-negotiable, and the olive oil drizzle should be tiny but confident.
